summary:
Imagine a smallholder Thai farmer with healthy, thriving crops—yet when drought looms seven days ahead or a loan is needed to survive the season, the bank still says no because there is no traditional collateral, while the farmer struggles with complicated charts and technical jargon.

What if satellite data from orbit could prove a Thai farmer is ready for a loan before the harvest even begins?

For Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, I developed CropShield—a dual-role web prototype bridging NASA Earth observation concepts (such as NASA POWER soil moisture and climate trends) with agricultural finance and farmer adaptation for Thai farmers. Instead of raw satellite jargon, CropShield translates data into a 0–100 Farm Health Score and a 7-day early risk forecast. Older Thai farmers get a clean, high-contrast interface with large text, distinct icons, and simple action cues, while BAAC (Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives) loan officers get a separate portfolio console featuring a farm plot map, installment timestamps, repayment countdowns, and an AI SMS assistant.

By turning satellite signals into data-backed risk and cash-flow visibility, CropShield helps Thai farmers act 7 days ahead and enables BAAC to evaluate tranche lending and parametric insurance—making rural finance fairer, faster, and more resilient.
details:
CropShield is a web application prototype built for Thai farmers and loan officers from the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives (BAAC). Most people today use smartphones, so building a web app makes access simple and familiar. At the same time, we noticed an important reality in Thailand: older farmers aged 65 and above make up a growing share of agricultural holders, and many are not comfortable using complex apps. To solve this, CropShield works in two separate roles—Farmer and BAAC Officer—while also sending SMS alerts for urgent 7-day warnings so older farmers do not even need to open the app, plus options to save records as a PDF or image on their device.

How it started:

It began after seeing news about UPOV 1991, which led me to look closer at the reality Thai farmers face. Many farmers carry heavy formal and informal debt because they have to borrow money every planting season just to fund the next crop. That raised a bold question: what if farmers could use a legal, practical form of collateral—without needing high-value assets—that a bank can actually verify? Even if this does not directly fix farmer income overnight, could we at least help them build verifiable data-backed collateral so they can borrow legally and safely?

How it works and what it does:

We connected Google AI Studio with NASA POWER agricultural and meteorological data to turn complex weather and soil information into clear, visual signals. Instead of raw technical numbers, farmers see a 0–100 Farm Health Score, a 7-day risk forecast, soil moisture cues, and simple action tips. For BAAC officers, the console provides a clean map view, installment schedules with clear dates and times, repayment countdowns, an AI SMS helper, and verifiable PDF records so officers can review and approve budgets without always visiting every farm in person.

Creativity, benefits, and intended impact:

What makes CropShield creative is connecting NASA Earth observation signals with practical farm adaptation and rural finance. Rather than treating satellite data as a standalone chart, it helps Thai farmers prepare 7 days ahead and gives BAAC officers clearer data to support tranche lending and risk checks. Over time, this can reduce manual field visits, speed up support, and make agricultural finance fairer and more resilient.

Tools and team behind Macrohard:

Macrohard is a solo team of one. Because time was limited to 48 hours, using AI tools to help build and design the application saved a lot of effort and allowed me to focus on business logic, user experience, and storytelling. I used Google AI Studio together with NASA POWER agricultural and climate data to prototype the app, designing large text, clear icons, and visual cards for older farmers, and a calm, easy-to-manage workspace for BAAC officers.
